```{r,evaluate=FALSE}
#defining the function
get_summary_DataExtracted<-function(column_name,df){
  uniq_vals<-df[!duplicated(df[,"study_id"]),][[column_name]] #getting 1st unique row per study and taking the column of interest
  
  #removing NAs, i.e. studies without information on that variable
  uniq_vals<-uniq_vals[!is.na(uniq_vals)]

  #CIs using Rmisc CI() function
  CI=CI(uniq_vals)
  
  res=list(Mean=mean(uniq_vals),
           SD=sd(uniq_vals),
           Median=median(uniq_vals),
           quantile95 = quantile(uniq_vals,c(0.025,0.975)),
           range=range(uniq_vals),
           Number_of_values=length(uniq_vals))
  
  return(res)}
```

# ########################################

# Statistical Models

# Main model

## main Model, frequentist
- the main Model, defined in M_main below, has three levels.
- the levels:
    - 1st = sampling variance (specified in V=es_var)
    - 2nd = intercept for each estimates
    - 3rd = pooling by studies
- all Models use a Normal distribution as the likelihood, so that es_i ~ Normal(Mu_i,sigma). 
- fitted with restricted maximum likelihood estimation.
    
### interpretation of estimate: 
_Positive values mean that cognitive performance in the satiated state is higher than in the fasted state._ 
_Negative values mean that cognitive performance in the fasted state is higher than in the satiated state._


```{r} 
fM_main <- rma.mv(yi = es,                # the Hedge's g values
                V = es_var,              # the variance around the estimate
                data = df,
                method = "REML",         # restricted maximum likelihood
                level = 95,              # 95% CI
                digits = 5,              # decimal points
                slab = ref,              # study labels
                tdist=TRUE,              # to use the Knapp-Hartung correction
                
             # Multilevel Model to handle sample dependency   
                random = ~1 | study_id/es_id #es_id clustered by study_id
             ) 
summary(fM_main)
```

### frequentist I^2
```{r}
W <- diag(1/df$es_var)
X <- model.matrix(fM_main)
# W and X need to have same dimensions
c(dim(W), dim(X))
P <- W - W %*% X %*% solve(t(X) %*% W %*% X) %*% t(X) %*% W
I2_statistic <- 100 * sum(fM_main$sigma2) / (sum(fM_main$sigma2) + 
                                                 (fM_main$k-fM_main$p)/sum(diag(P)))
print(c("I^2:",I2_statistic))
```


## bayesian approach using brms

### prior elicidation
```{r}
plot(density(rnorm(1e4,mean=0,sd=1)),main="prior for intercept")
plot(density(rhcauchy(1e4,sigma=0.5)),xlim=c(0,80),main="prior for SDs")
```


```{r}
#priors
priors <- c(prior(normal(0,1), class = Intercept),
            prior(cauchy(0,0.5), class = sd))
# effect sizes = es, es_var = variance/SE, study_id = study level 
bM_main = brm("es | se(es_var) ~ 1 + (1|study_id/es_id)",
              prior=priors,
              data= df,
              iter=4000, #Rhat & ESS not good with default -> go up
              save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
              file="bM_main",
              file_refit = "on_change"
              )
#saveRDS(bM_main,"bM_main.RDS")        
```

```{r}
#bM_main = readRDS("bM_main.RDS")
summary(bM_main)

## the estimated random effects for eache stiamte within studies
#ranef(bM_main)$`study_id:es_id`

##estimated random effects for each study-cluster
study_ranef = data.frame(ranef(bM_main)$`study_id`)
#median(study_ranef$Estimate.Intercept)

bM_main_draws = as_draws_df(bM_main)

#percentage of draws below zero, indicating higher performance of fasted
count(bM_main_draws$Intercept<0)
sum(bM_main_draws$Intercept<0)/length(bM_main_draws$Intercept)

```
for intercept, Rhat was initially too high with 1.05 (assume 1.01 as acceptance threshold, based on STAN recommendation) & especially bulk ESS too low -> doubled iterations from default -> Rhat acceptable, ESS better.
Vehtari: if R-hat & ESS improve by increasing iter, no need to worry (https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/low-ess-and-high-rhat-for-random-intercept-slope-simulation-rstan-and-rstanarm/9985/7)

## extracting samples
 sd_study_id__Intercept for the between-study heterogeneity τ on study level.
```{r}
post_samples = as.data.frame(bM_main,variable= c("b_Intercept", "sd_study_id__Intercept","sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept")) 
```

### plotting posterior samples
making 3 rows * 2 cols grid with posterior density in one column, chains in the other for Intercept, sd on both levels
```{r}
######## posterior densitiy plots:
p_Intercept_pd = ggplot(aes(x = b_Intercept), data = post_samples) +
    geom_density(fill = cbPalette[1],                # set the color
               color = cbPalette[1], alpha = 0.7) +  
  geom_point(y = 0,                               # add point at mean
             x = median(post_samples$b_Intercept)) +
  ylim(0,15)+
  #add vertical line for zero
  geom_vline(xintercept=0,lty=2)+
  labs(x = expression(alpha),
       y = expression(Density),
       title="A. Intercept") +
  apatheme

p_sd_study_pd = ggplot(aes(x = sd_study_id__Intercept), data = post_samples) +
  geom_density(fill = cbPalette[3],               # set the color
               color = cbPalette[3], alpha = 0.7) +  
  # add point at mean
  geom_point(y = 0, 
             x = median(post_samples$sd_study_id__Intercept)) +        
  xlim(0,0.5)+ ylim(0,15)+
  
    labs(x = expression(tau), #expression(tau*" study level")
       y = expression(Density),
       title="B. SD study") +
  apatheme

p_sd_es_pd = ggplot(aes(x = `sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept`), data = post_samples) +
  geom_density(fill = cbPalette[5],               # set the color
               color = cbPalette[5], alpha = 0.7) +  
  geom_point(y = 0, # add point at mean
             x = median(post_samples$`sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept`)) + 
  xlim(0,0.5)+ylim(0,16)+
    labs(x = expression(tau),#expression(tau*" estimate level")
       y =expression(Density),
       title = "C. SD es") +
  apatheme

######## trace plots:
# getting trace data in nice format for plotting
p_trace_data = mcmc_trace_data(bM_main,pars=c("b_Intercept","sd_study_id__Intercept","sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept"))
p_trace_data$chain = factor(p_trace_data$chain)
unique(p_trace_data$warmup)#no warm-up data in there - good

## plotting intercept trace
p_Intercept_trace = ggplot(data=subset(p_trace_data,parameter=="b_Intercept"),
       aes(x=iteration,y=value,colour=chain))+
  geom_line()+scale_colour_manual(values=alpha(c(cbPalette[1],cbPalette[3],cbPalette[5],cbPalette[7]),0.6))+
  xlab("Iteration")+ylab("Value")+ apatheme
#p_Intercept_trace

#sd on study level trace
p_sd_study_trace = ggplot(data=subset(p_trace_data,parameter=="sd_study_id__Intercept"),
       aes(x=iteration,y=value,colour=chain))+
  geom_line()+scale_colour_manual(values=alpha(c(cbPalette[1],cbPalette[3],cbPalette[5],cbPalette[7]),0.6))+
  xlab("Iteration")+ylab("Value")+ apatheme
#p_sd_study_trace

#sd on es level trace
p_sd_es_trace = ggplot(data=subset(p_trace_data,parameter=="sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept"),
       aes(x=iteration,y=value,colour=chain))+
  geom_line()+scale_colour_manual(values=alpha(c(cbPalette[1],cbPalette[3],cbPalette[5],cbPalette[7]),0.6))+
  xlab("Iteration")+ylab("Value")+ apatheme
#p_sd_es_trace


grid.arrange(p_Intercept_pd,p_Intercept_trace,
             p_sd_study_pd,p_sd_study_trace,
             p_sd_es_pd,p_sd_es_trace, nrow=3,ncol=2)

##    -- .tiff file for publication  --
tiff(filename = "./data/main_model_posterior.tiff", 
    width = 16, height = 12.8, 
    pointsize = 12, res = 300,units ="cm")
grid.arrange(p_Intercept_pd,p_Intercept_trace,
             p_sd_study_pd,p_sd_study_trace,
             p_sd_es_pd,p_sd_es_trace, nrow=3,ncol=2)
dev.off()

png(filename = "./data/main_model_posterior.png", 
    width = 16, height = 12.8, 
    pointsize = 12, res = 300,units ="cm")
grid.arrange(p_Intercept_pd,p_Intercept_trace,
             p_sd_study_pd,p_sd_study_trace,
             p_sd_es_pd,p_sd_es_trace, nrow=3,ncol=2)
dev.off()

```

### posterior draws cognitive domain
```{r}
posterior_cog = as.data.frame(bM_cog,variable= c("b_Intercept", "b_cognitive_domaincognitive_flexibility","b_cognitive_domaingeneral_executive_function", "b_cognitive_domaininhibitory_control","b_cognitive_domainlongMterm_memory","b_cognitive_domainperceptual_accuracy","b_cognitive_domainworking_memory",
                                                    "sd_study_id__Intercept","sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept")) 
#shortening column names
names(posterior_cog) <- gsub("b_cognitive_domain", "b_", names(posterior_cog))


#calculating values by adding coefficients to Intercept
posterior_cog$attention = posterior_cog$b_Intercept
posterior_cog$cognitive_flexibility = posterior_cog$b_Intercept+posterior_cog$b_cognitive_flexibility
posterior_cog$general_executive_function = posterior_cog$b_Intercept+posterior_cog$b_general_executive_function
posterior_cog$inhibitory_control = posterior_cog$b_Intercept + posterior_cog$b_inhibitory_control
posterior_cog$long_term_memory = posterior_cog$b_Intercept +posterior_cog$b_longMterm_memory
posterior_cog$perceptual_accuracy = posterior_cog$b_Intercept + posterior_cog$b_perceptual_accuracy
posterior_cog$working_memory =  posterior_cog$b_Intercept + posterior_cog$b_working_memory 

## calculating median, SE  and 95% Cred Int


posterior_cog_4plot = pivot_longer(posterior_cog,cols=c("attention","cognitive_flexibility","general_executive_function","inhibitory_control","long_term_memory","perceptual_accuracy","working_memory"))
```

### alternative cross-classified model for study & cog domain
_benefit: can see how much variance is explained by difference between studies and how much by difference between cognitive domains of outcome_
```{r}
priors <- c(prior(normal(0,1), class = Intercept),
            prior(cauchy(0,0.5), class = sd))

bM_cog_alt = brm("es | se(es_var) ~ 1 +  (1|study_id/es_id) +(1|cognitive_domain)",
              prior=priors,
              data= df,
              iter=4000,
             file="bM_cog_alt",file_refit="on_change")

summary(bM_cog_alt)
```
-> splits the variance over the study/es_id and the different outcome domains

plotting the variance:
```{r}
#label <-
#  tibble(tau   = c(.13, .16),
#         y     = c(15, 10),
#         label = c("sigma['cognitive_domain']", "sigma['study_id']"))

# wrangle

posterior_samples_cog_cross_var = posterior_samples(bM_cog_alt) %>% 
        select(starts_with("sd")) %>% 
        gather(variance, tau) %>% 
        mutate(variance = str_remove(variance, "sd_") %>% str_remove(., "__Intercept")) 
  
  # plot
crossclassplot = ggplot(data = posterior_samples_cog_cross_var, aes(x = tau)) +
  geom_density(aes(fill = variance), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cbPalette, 
                    labels = c("cognitive domain", "study id", "es id")) + 
  apatheme + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

dev.off()
```

#### spelling out the interactions
since we have 2 categorical variables, the interaction is a simple addition
```{r}
posterior_cog_food = as.data.frame(bM_multi_cog_binary_food_inter,variable= c("b_Intercept", "b_cognitive_domaincognitive_flexibility","b_cognitive_domaingeneral_executive_function", "b_cognitive_domaininhibitory_control","b_cognitive_domainlongMterm_memory","b_cognitive_domainperceptual_accuracy","b_cognitive_domainworking_memory",
"b_binary_foodyes", "b_cognitive_domaincognitive_flexibility:binary_foodyes","b_cognitive_domaingeneral_executive_function:binary_foodyes", "b_cognitive_domaininhibitory_control:binary_foodyes","b_cognitive_domainlongMterm_memory:binary_foodyes","b_cognitive_domainperceptual_accuracy:binary_foodyes","b_cognitive_domainworking_memory:binary_foodyes",
                                                    "sd_study_id__Intercept","sd_study_id:es_id__Intercept")) 
#shortening column names
names(posterior_cog_food) <- gsub("b_cognitive_domain", "b_", names(posterior_cog_food))
#View(posterior_cog_food)

#calculating values by spelling out interaction coefficients
posterior_cog_food$attention_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept #intercept is attention (as for initial cog domain model)*no food
posterior_cog_food$attention_food = posterior_cog_food$b_binary_foodyes #going from intercept (attention + no food) to food -> attention+food

posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_cognitive_flexibility
posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_food = posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_cognitive_flexibility:binary_foodyes`
#control:
#median(posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_nofood)
#median(posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_food)
#abs(median(posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_nofood))+median(posterior_cog_food$cognitive_flexibility_food)
posterior_cog_food$general_executive_function_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_general_executive_function
posterior_cog_food$general_executive_function_food = posterior_cog_food$general_executive_function_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_general_executive_function:binary_foodyes`

posterior_cog_food$inhibitory_control_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_inhibitory_control
posterior_cog_food$inhibitory_control_food = posterior_cog_food$inhibitory_control_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_inhibitory_control:binary_foodyes`

posterior_cog_food$long_term_memory_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_longMterm_memory
posterior_cog_food$long_term_memory_food = posterior_cog_food$long_term_memory_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_longMterm_memory:binary_foodyes`

posterior_cog_food$perceptual_accuracy_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_perceptual_accuracy
posterior_cog_food$perceptual_accuracy_food = posterior_cog_food$perceptual_accuracy_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_perceptual_accuracy:binary_foodyes`

posterior_cog_food$working_memory_nofood = posterior_cog_food$b_Intercept+posterior_cog_food$b_working_memory
posterior_cog_food$working_memory_food = posterior_cog_food$working_memory_nofood + posterior_cog_food$`b_working_memory:binary_foodyes`


```

### funnel plot for study type

#### creating funnel plot basis
__se calculation may be wrong but plot looks exactly like with frequentist approach__
```{r}
#extracting coefficient from study_id level
fp_base_data=data.frame(coef(bM_main, robust = T)$study_id[,,"Intercept"])

#storing values from main model
estimate<-median(fp_base_data$Estimate)
# SE interpreted as Estimate Error 
se<-median(fp_base_data$Est.Error)

#sequence of sampling variance values
se.seq=seq(0, max(df$es_var), 0.001)

# generating 95%CI and 99%CI boundaries
ll95 = estimate-(1.96*se.seq)
ul95 = estimate+(1.96*se.seq)
ll99 = estimate-(3.29*se.seq)
ul99 = estimate+(3.29*se.seq)
#CI for estimate
meanll95 = estimate-(1.96*se)
meanul95 = estimate+(1.96*se)

funplot_graphical<-data.frame(ll95,ul95,ll99,ul99,meanll95,meanul95)
```

## Leave-one-group-out analysis
Bayesian way
```{r}
## initialize df
bMLOO_res_m <-matrix(data=NA,
                 nrow=length(unique(df$study_id)),    #length of the number of studies
                 ncol=10,
                  dimnames=list(NULL,c("s_left_out","ref","coeff","se","ci.lb","ci.ub","R_hat","Bulk_ESS","Tail_ESS","N_df_i")))

##setting idex for result df
ind=1
## for each study id
#looping through all studies, to remove them one by one:
for (SID in sort(unique(df$study_id))){#for  every study
  #[1:4]
 # selecting the data not in the to-be-exlcuded study
  df_i = df[df$study_id!=SID,]
  
# make variable for name 
  model_name_for_storage = paste0("bM_LOO_study_",SID)   
  Mi = update(
              #take the main model
              bM_main,
              #refit to reduced data
              newdata=df_i,
              iter=4000,                                                  # <- set iterations here
              # store it as bM_LOO_studyXX
              #file=model_name_for_storage,
              #file_refit="always"
              )

  # get summary values on right level
  ms = summary(Mi)$fixed
# add point estimates, 95% and diagnostics to df
  Mi_res = c(
    SID,
    unique(df[df$study_id==SID,]$ref),
    ms$Estimate, #Estimate
    ms$Est.Error, #SE
    ms$`l-95% CI`, #ci.lb
    ms$`u-95% CI`, #ci.ub
    ms$Rhat, #R-hat
    ms$Bulk_ESS, # ESS
    ms$Tail_ESS,
    #adding the combined sample size for later use
    sum(df_i[!duplicated(df_i[,"study_id"]),]$N)
  )  
  bMLOO_res_m[ind,] = Mi_res
  
  ind=ind+1
}

bMLOO_res = data.frame(bMLOO_res_m)



# adding main estimate
ms_main = summary(bM_main)$fixed
main_res = data.frame(s_left_out=0,
    ref="Main model",
    coeff=ms_main$Estimate, #Estimate
    se = ms_main$Est.Error, #SE
    ci.lb = ms_main$`l-95% CI`, #ci.lb
    ci.ub = ms_main$`u-95% CI`, #ci.ub
    R_hat = ms_main$Rhat, #R-hat
    Bulk_ESS = ms_main$Bulk_ESS, # ESS
    Tail_ESS = ms_main$Tail_ESS,
    N_df_i = sum(df[!duplicated(df[,"study_id"]),]$N)
  )

# for plotting order:
#bMLOO_res$order = 1:nrow(bMLOO_res)+1

bMLOO_res$coeff = as.numeric(bMLOO_res$coeff)

#arranging according to coeff
bMLOO_res = plyr::arrange(bMLOO_res,-coeff)

#adding main estimate
bMLOO_res = rbind(bMLOO_res,main_res)
#fixating order
bMLOO_res$plot_order<-1:nrow(bMLOO_res)
head(bMLOO_res)

#dtype
bMLOO_res$LOO_or_main = factor(ifelse(bMLOO_res$ref=="Main model",0,1))
bMLOO_res$ci.ub = as.numeric(bMLOO_res$ci.ub)
bMLOO_res$ci.lb = as.numeric(bMLOO_res$ci.lb)



saveRDS(bMLOO_res,"bMLOO_res.RDS")
bMLOO_res = readRDS("bmLOO_res.RDS")


```

### calculate MSE between LOO and main model

```{r}
#getting Main Model estimate
MM = subset(bMLOO_res,ref=="Main model")$coeff
#getting LOO estimates
LOOs = subset(bMLOO_res,ref!="Main model")$coeff

#calculating MSE by  getting distance, squaring, summing, dividing by N
dist_LOO_MM = LOOs-MM
dist_LOO_MM_sq = dist_LOO_MM^2
MSE_LOO_MM = sum(dist_LOO_MM_sq)/length(dist_LOO_MM_sq)
RMSE_LOO_MM = sqrt(MSE_LOO_MM)
print(paste("root mean squared error LOOs to main model:",RMSE_LOO_MM))
```
MSE means the average distance between the full model and the reduced models.

# sensitivity analyses 
## for main model
```{r}
#library(brms)
#library(dplyr)

# Define a list of different priors for the Intercept with varying standard deviations

prior_list = list(
  c(prior(normal(0, 0.1), class = Intercept), 
    prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd)),
    c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept), 
    prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd)),
    c(prior(normal(0, 10), class = Intercept), 
    prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd)),
    c(prior(normal(0, 100), class = Intercept), 
    prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd)))

prior_list[[2]]
# Initialize an empty dataframe to store the posterior draws
posterior_draws_df <- data.frame()

# Loop over each set of priors
for (i in seq_along(prior_list)) {
  # Define the model name for each set of priors
  model_name <- paste0("Model_", i)
  print(prior_list[[i]])
  # Run the brms model with the current set of priors
  bM_main <- brm(
    formula = es | se(es_var) ~ 1 + (1|study_id/es_id),
    prior = prior_list[[i]],
    data = df,
    iter = 4000, 
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    file = model_name,
    file_refit = "on_change"
  )
  
  # Extract posterior draws
  draws <- as_draws_df(bM_main)
  
  # Add a column to indicate which model the draws are from
  draws$model <- model_name
  
  # add the sd for the intercept prior
  #draws$intercept_prior_sd <- prior_list[[i]][[1]]$args[[2]]
  
  # Bind the new draws to the existing dataframe
  posterior_draws_df <- bind_rows(posterior_draws_df, draws)
}

# Display the combined posterior draws dataframe
print(posterior_draws_df)

#posterior_draws_df$model
posterior_draws_df$SD_prior_intercept = ifelse(
  posterior_draws_df$model=="Model_1", 0.1,
  ifelse(
  posterior_draws_df$model=="Model_2", 1,
  ifelse(
  posterior_draws_df$model=="Model_3", 10,
  100)))
```

```{r}
  # Run the brms model with the current set of priors

  bM_cog = brm("es | se(es_var) ~ 1 + cognitive_domain + (1|study_id/es_id)",

}
```

## calculating score for agreement

```{r}
# cognitive domain
```
